historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term blended forward rate (FY29-FY32 base path), not the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR 44.9% vs equity 3yr CAGR 24.3% diverges >30%: FY2023 EPS base was depressed (Rs 14.57) and FY2025 carried a one-off Indus consolidation gain. Equity CAGR is itself inflated by capital inflows (Rs 157bn partly-paid call FY26, Rs 282bn ICIL allotment FY27) and by Indus consolidation, so neither is a clean organic growth anchor. Revenue CAGR (15-16%) also includes Indus consolidation from Nov-2024 and the Jul-2024 tariff hike.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on reported FCF less SBC (lease cash is not consistently extractable before FY2024, so the full treatment-B series starts at FY2024: owner FCF FY24 ~Rs 275bn, FY25 ~Rs 473bn, FY26 Rs 644bn). EPS 5yr CAGR is undefined because FY2021 EPS was negative (Rs -27.52, AGR provisions). SBC is 0.15% of revenue and does not distort the FCF series.

scenario_narratives.base: India mobile premiumisation continues (ARPU Rs 271 in Q2 FY27, record postpaid adds) and the industry's next 12-15% tariff hike arrives in FY28, taking consolidated growth to 11% that year before decelerating to 4.5% by FY36; EBITDA margin edges from 57.5% to 60% as fixed network and lease costs are spread over tariff-led revenue; Africa compounds in constant currency with FX roughly neutral; capex intensity moderates from 24% to 20% of revenue including a ~3pp spectrum-renewal allowance; cash tax normalises from ~20% to 27% as India losses are exhausted. Terminal value is bound by the 15x owner-FCF cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: A larger (15-20%) tariff hike lands early in FY28 and a second round follows by FY30 as Vodafone Idea's erosion funnels high-value customers to Airtel; Homes/FWA (>3,300 cities), Airtel Business, Nxtra (1 GW ambition) and Financial Services scale with high incremental margins toward a 62.5% consolidated EBITDA margin; Africa delivers 20%+ constant-currency growth with the naira stable so reported growth matches; capex intensity falls to 18.5% as the 5G build matures. Terminal 17x cap binds.
scenario_narratives.bear: Reliance Jio, with Reliance Industries' balance sheet behind it, reopens the price war to defend volume share and the tariff hike never comes; a renewed African currency shock (naira, kwacha) repeats the FY24-25 reported-revenue collapse; the Supreme Court denies Airtel's AGR waiver while Vodafone Idea gets relief, leaving the Rs 330bn AGR liability intact; capex stays above 22% of revenue as 5G/fibre/data-centre spend fails to moderate and margins drift back to 55%. Terminal 13x cap binds; the business still survives comfortably at 0.7x ex-lease leverage.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on consolidated INR flows with leases charged as an operating cost, spectrum renewals charged as capex, cash taxes ramped to normal, and the large listed minorities (Airtel Africa, Indus Towers, Bharti Hexacom) deducted at market value rather than book. The model is deliberately strict on three things the market tends to wave through: the ~Rs 135bn/yr of lease cash that IFRS 16 moves out of EBITDA, the ~Rs 1.3tn of minority value inside the consolidated EBITDA, and the end of the India tax shelter. A terminal cap of 15x owner FCF (~6x EBITDA) is the house stance for a mature telco and binds in every scenario; the Gordon value at 10%/4% would be ~15% higher.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal cap: every scenario binds at the FCF-multiple cap; a reader who believes a mature Indian telco deserves the Gordon multiple (17x owner FCF at 10%/4%) should add ~15% to the base value
NCI at market: ~Rs 1.29tn (Rs 207/share) is deducted; if Indus or Airtel Africa are themselves undervalued this is a conservative bias, and the Airtel Africa share count is an estimate
Spectrum allowance (~3pp of revenue inside capex) is a judgment on renewal timing; FY2032-36 renewals could be cheaper or dearer than assumed
Tariff hike timing: the base case assumes one 12-15% hike in FY28; a delay to FY29 removes ~1 year of margin uplift
Africa FX: USD-reported earnings in local-currency markets; a repeat of the FY24-25 naira devaluation is the bear case
AGR litigation: Rs 330bn deferred AGR liability sits in net debt; a waiver would be upside, an adverse re-computation downside
Lease treatment: consolidated ROU depreciation is estimated (~Rs 95bn) for the tax line; a Rs 15bn error moves value by well under Rs 1/share

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (NSE regular close); 52-week range 1,726.3-2,174.5. Subsidiary marks: AAF.L, INDUSTOWER.NS, BHARTIHEXA.NS and GBPINR=X from the same endpoint on 2026-11-06/07.
data_sources.financials: BHARTIARTL.NS_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (INR millions, FY2017-FY2026 annual and Q4 FY21-Q2 FY27 quarterly); FY2026 Integrated Annual Report (Extracted/BHARTIARTL.NS_Annual_FY2026.txt) for lease cash, NCI, deferred payment liabilities, subsidiary stakes and share capital; Q1/Q2 FY27 quarterly reports and presentations for the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet, share count and guidance.
data_sources.qualitative: BHARTIARTL.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): segment mix, competitive position, Q2 FY27 results and guidance, bull/bear axes.

inputs.share_count_basis: 6,241m shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27 quarterly report, incl. 0.65m partly-paid shares suspended from trading). The step from 6,094m (Mar-2026) is NON-SBC issuance already in the count: 146.76m fully paid shares allotted to Indian Continental Investment Ltd at ~Rs 1,923/share in Q1 FY27 (Q1 FY27 report line 172) plus the first-and-final call of Rs 401.25 on 391.2m partly-paid rights shares completed in FY26. ESOP dilution is immaterial (diluted EPS = basic EPS to two decimals), so the diluted count is taken as 6,241m and held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings Rs 1,212,303m less cash & current investments Rs 329,532m at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY27). Borrowings INCLUDE the deferred payment liabilities to DoT for spectrum (~Rs 530bn) and for AGR dues (~Rs 330bn at Mar-2026; FY26 AR note 17.1), so the AGR overhang is already in the bridge. Lease liabilities of Rs 783,034m are EXCLUDED because leases are charged inside the flows (treatment B). Check: company-reported net debt Rs 1,665,800m less leases Rs 783,034m = Rs 882,766m, ties to Rs 5m.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY2026 = reported FCF (OCF 1,222,296 less reported capex 440,076 = 782,220) less SBC 3,157 less interest income 0 less lease cash 134,702 (principal 67,197 in financing + interest on lease liabilities 67,505; FY26 AR consolidated cash-flow lines 18420 and 22378). The lease deduction is the treatment-(B) adjustment of owner-fcf-adaptations.md part (b); it is not in the generic three-term formula and is stated here so the identity can be reconstructed.
inputs.sbc_source: Consolidated share-based payment expense FY2026 Rs 3,157m (sum of quarterly reports; standalone AR line 17072 shows Rs 380m, the balance is Airtel Africa, Indus Towers and Hexacom schemes). No equity-award tax withholding disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). Effectively an SBC-zero market: 0.15% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 finance income Rs 11,158m is NOT stripped: the company is a net borrower (net debt 0.7x EBITDAaL), the cash is netted against debt in the bridge, and finance income sits below EBITDA so it never enters the component build.
inputs.buyback_note: Rs 1,447m FY2026 treasury-share purchases by the ESOP trust (AR line 18364) -- the flat share count is a modelling convention, not funded by repurchases; the company is a dividend payer (Rs 113bn paid FY26, Rs 24/share declared).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T09:59:12Z regular NSE close (Friday); valuation date 2026-11-08 is a Sunday, so this is the latest close and is not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% risk-free, India ERP ~5.5%, beta ~0.75 for a defensive duopoly telco gives cost of equity ~10.6%; after-tax cost of debt ~5.5% on INR borrowings at 7.2-7.8% (AR note 17.1); ex-lease debt is ~6% of EV so WACC ~10.2%, rounded to 10.0%. Held identical across scenarios -- risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows (adaptations part f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash (principal + interest, Rs 134,702m FY26 = 6.4% of revenue) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, lease liabilities (Rs 783bn) are excluded from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (total D&A Rs 527,108m less estimated consolidated ROU depreciation ~Rs 95bn; standalone ROU depreciation disclosed at Rs 63,988m, AR line 16507; Africa/Indus add the balance) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI is deducted ONCE, in the equity bridge, at market value rather than book. NCI took 21% of FY26 profit (total Rs 338,228m vs attributable Rs 266,952m) and book NCI is only Rs 469,068m (Mar-2026), far below the market value of the minorities: Airtel Africa 37.38% not owned (Bharti 62.62%, AR line 20036), Indus Towers 48.74% (Bharti 51.256%, AR line 23420), Bharti Hexacom 30% (AR line 23431), plus Nxtra (Carlyle ~24%) and other unlisted NCI at an estimate. Associates (Robi Axiata ~28%, Dialog ~10%) are equity-accounted, outside EBITDA, and added back at approximate market under the matching-asset rule.
inputs.capex_note: Reported capex FY26 Rs 440,076m = 20.9% of revenue; H1 FY27 ran at 23.2% (Rs 276,820m) including Nxtra data-centre land. The capex_pct_path is INCLUSIVE of a ~3pp-of-revenue allowance for future spectrum acquisitions/renewals (Airtel bought ~Rs 830bn of spectrum over the last decade, ~Rs 83bn/yr; the 2012-2016 Indian spectrum tranches renew in FY2032-36, inside the horizon) which the reported capex line excludes. Existing spectrum/AGR deferred liabilities are already in net debt and are not charged again.
inputs.tax_note: FY26 cash tax Rs 62,839m was ~10% of component EBIT because India losses were still being absorbed; H1 FY27 cash tax jumped to Rs 76,255m (~20% of EBIT) as the shelter ran out. Paths ramp to a blended normal of ~27% (India 25.17% new regime on ~70% of profit, Africa effective 35-40% on the rest). The tax shelter is not perpetuated.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping through FY31 on tariff-led ARPU). Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md: integrated operating telco (India mobile 51%, Africa 31%, Indus towers 14%, Airtel Business 10%, Homes 4%) -- not a REIT, bank or holdco, so owner-FCF applies with the non-US adaptations: INR WACC, lease treatment (B), NCI at market in the bridge, associates added back, SBC-zero band collapse. No prior DCF or memory entry; this is a fresh build. FY0 is FY2026 (Mar-2026); year 1 = FY2027, of which H1 is already reported (+17.5% YoY revenue). Price is NSE INR and the flows are INR so no FX bridge. Terminal value binds at the cap in every scenario (Gordon at 10%/4% would be 17.3x owner FCF; cap 15x base is ~6x terminal EBITDA, the house stance for a mature telco).

bear.narrative: Jio reopens the price war to defend volume share and the expected tariff hike is deferred indefinitely; a fresh naira/kwacha devaluation cuts Africa's reported revenue; the AGR waiver plea is denied with no parity relief; capex stays above 22% of revenue as 5G, fibre and data-centre spend fail to moderate; margins drift back to 55%.

base.narrative: FY27 +16% (H1 already +17.5%, Q2 +4% QoQ); the brokerage-flagged 12-15% India tariff hike lands in FY28 lifting growth to 11% and EBITDA margin toward 60%; Africa grows double-digit in constant currency with the naira stable; capex intensity moderates from 24% to 20% of revenue (incl. ~3pp spectrum allowance); cash tax normalises to 27% by FY32.

bull.narrative: Tariff hike of 15-20% lands early FY28 and a second round follows by FY30 as Vodafone Idea keeps ceding high-ARPU subscribers; Homes/FWA, Airtel Business, Nxtra and Financial Services scale at high incremental margins; Africa delivers 20%+ constant-currency growth with reported-currency parity; capex intensity falls below 19% as 5G rollout matures.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bull weight is cut because the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once -- a competitor-dependent tariff hike, African currency stability, and capex moderation while four new growth engines are being funded. Bear weight is raised above default for the two exogenous, high-severity risks in the Analysis JSON (Jio price war; Africa FX, which cut Nigeria revenue 40% in one year) even though there is no going-concern risk at 0.7x net debt/EBITDAaL ex-leases.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
